customer: I've torn the house apart looking for the title to my SUV and I can't find it anywhere, and with a newborn I really don't have time for this. I'm in Virginia and want to sell the car to you before the baby's car seat stuff gets any more complicated. Do I need to order a replacement title before I can even book an appointment?
agent: Good news, you can stop searching, because Virginia uses electronic titles, so your title is a record held by the state rather than a paper document. That means there's no paper title to bring when you sell your SUV; we transfer the title electronically at your appointment. If you had a loan on the vehicle, the lender releases the lien electronically as well, and our article "My loan is paid off but the lien is still on the title" covers that situation if it applies to you.
